title_en: Notice of the Supreme People's Court, the Supreme People's Procuratorate, the Ministry of Public Security, and the Ministry of Justice on Printing and Issuing the Opinions on Handling Criminal Cases Involving Sexual Assault of Minors
keywords_en: rape; organizing prostitution; criminal cases of sexual assault against minors
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court Supreme People's Procuratorate Ministry of Public Security Ministry of Justice

Notice on Issuing the "Opinions on Handling Criminal Cases of Sexual Assault against Minors"

Gao Jian Fa [2023] No. 4

High People's Courts, People's Procuratorates, Public Security Departments (Bureaus), and Justice Departments (Bureaus) of all provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government; Military Court of the People's Liberation Army, Military Procuratorate of the People's Liberation Army; Production and Construction Corps Branch of the High People's Court of Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region; People's Procuratorate, Public Security Bureau, and Justice Bureau of Xinjiang Production and Construction Corps:

For the purposes of thoroughly studying and implementing the spirit of the 20th National Congress of the Communist Party of China, fully implementing Xi Jinping Thought on the Rule of Law, punishing crimes of sexual assault against minors according to law, further improving the quality and efficiency of handling criminal cases of sexual assault against minors, and strengthening the judicial protection of minors, in accordance with the Criminal Law of the People's Republic of China, the Criminal Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the Law of the People's Republic of China on the Protection of Minors, and other legal provisions, the Supreme People's Court, the Supreme People's Procuratorate, the Ministry of Public Security, and the Ministry of Justice have formulated the "Opinions on Handling Criminal Cases of Sexual Assault against Minors," which are hereby issued for your earnest implementation.

May 24, 2023

Opinions on Handling Criminal Cases of Sexual Assault against Minors

For the purposes of deeply implementing Xi Jinping Thought on the Rule of Law, punishing crimes of sexual assault against minors according to law, standardizing the handling of criminal cases of sexual assault against minors, and strengthening the judicial protection of minors, in accordance with the Criminal Law of the People's Republic of China, the Criminal Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the Law of the People's Republic of China on the Protection of Minors, and other relevant legal provisions, and in light of judicial practice, these Opinions are formulated.

I. General Principles

Article 1 The crimes of sexual assault against minors referred to in these Opinions include the crimes of rape against minors, the crime of sexual assault by persons with caregiving duties, the crime of forcible indecency or insult, the crime of child molestation, the crime of organizing prostitution, the crime of forcing prostitution, the crime of assisting in organizing prostitution, the crime of luring, tolerating, or introducing prostitution, and the crime of luring minors into prostitution, as prescribed in Articles 236, 236-1, 237, 358, and 359 of the Criminal Law of the People's Republic of China.

Article 2 The handling of criminal cases of sexual assault against minors shall adhere to the following principles:

(1) Severely punishing crimes of sexual assault against minors according to law;

(2) Adhering to the principle of best interests of the minor, fully considering that minors are not yet mature in physical and mental development and are susceptible to harm, and effectively protecting the legitimate rights and interests of minors;

(3) Adhering to the principle of dual protection: where a minor commits a crime of sexual assault against another minor, while protecting the legitimate rights and interests of the minor victim according to law, the legitimate rights and interests of the minor suspect and the minor defendant shall also be protected according to law.

Article 3 People's courts, people's procuratorates, and public security organs shall establish specialized institutions or designate specialized personnel who are familiar with the physical and mental characteristics of minors to be responsible for handling criminal cases of sexual assault against minors. Where the minor victim is female, female staff shall participate.

Legal aid agencies shall assign lawyers who are familiar with the physical and mental characteristics of minors to provide legal aid to minors.

Article 4 Where people's courts or people's procuratorates, in handling criminal cases of sexual assault against minors, discover loopholes in social governance, they shall issue judicial recommendations or procuratorial recommendations according to law.

People's procuratorates shall supervise, according to law, litigious activities involving sexual assault against minors, and shall promptly issue supervisory opinions where illegal circumstances are discovered. Where the legitimate rights and interests of minors are violated and involve the public interest, they shall initiate public interest litigation according to law.

II. Case Handling

Article 5 Upon receiving reports, complaints, or tips of sexual assault against a minor, the public security organ shall promptly accept and quickly review the matter. Where the conditions for criminal case filing are met, the public security organ shall immediately file the case for investigation. For major, difficult, or complex cases, the review period for case filing shall generally not exceed seven days. Where any of the following circumstances exist, the public security organ shall directly file the case for investigation after acceptance:

(1) A minor with significantly delayed mental development or a minor under the age of 14 becomes pregnant, terminates pregnancy, or gives birth;

(2) The reproductive organs or intimate parts of a minor suffer obviously abnormal injuries;

(3) A minor is organized, forced, lured, tolerated, or introduced into prostitution;

(4) Other evidence that a crime of sexual assault against a minor has occurred.

Article 6 Where the public security organ discovers that a minor may have been sexually assaulted or receives relevant leads, regardless of whether the case falls within its jurisdiction, it shall promptly take emergency measures such as stopping the assault, protecting the victim, and safeguarding the scene. Where necessary, it shall notify relevant departments to provide temporary shelter or assistance to the victim.

Article 7 After accepting a case, if upon review the public security organ finds that there are facts of a crime requiring criminal liability, but the jurisdiction is unclear due to an inability to determine the place of crime or the suspect, the public security organ that accepted the case shall first file the case for investigation. After clarifying jurisdiction through investigation, the case and evidentiary materials shall be promptly transferred to the public security organ with jurisdiction.

Article 8 People's procuratorates and public security organs handling criminal cases of sexual assault against minors shall adhere to the principles of division of labor with mutual cooperation and mutual checks, strengthen the supervision of and collaboration in investigations, and improve the mechanism for two-way information sharing to form a concerted effort. During the investigation process, the public security organ may consult with the people's procuratorate for opinions and suggestions on case characterization, evidence collection, application of law, and requirements for the protection of minors.

Article 9 Where a people's procuratorate considers that a public security organ should have filed a case for investigation but failed to do so, or where a victim or their legal representative, or a person with special duties of care towards the minor, raises an objection to the people's procuratorate on this basis, and upon review the grievance is reasonable, the people's procuratorate shall require the public security organ to explain the reasons for not filing the case. Where the people's procuratorate considers the reasons for not filing the case to be unfounded, it shall notify the public security organ to file the case, and the public security organ shall file the case upon receiving the notice.

Article 10 For adult criminal suspects or defendants who commit sexual assault against minors, the application of non-custodial compulsory measures shall be strictly controlled according to law, and prosecution and punishment shall be carried out strictly according to law.

Article 11 When public security organs handle criminal cases of sexual assault against minors, when submitting requests for approval of arrest or for transfer for prosecution, the case file materials shall include materials proving the source of the case and the course of the incident, as well as a description of the circumstances under which the suspect was brought to justice (or apprehended).

Article 12 When people's courts or people's procuratorates handle cases of sexual assault against minors, they shall promptly inform the minor victim and their legal representative or close relatives of their right to appoint a litigation representative, and inform them of their right to apply for legal aid according to law.

Article 13 When people's courts, people's procuratorates, or public security organs handle criminal cases of sexual assault against minors, unless there are circumstances that would hinder the handling of the case, they shall promptly inform the minor victim and their legal representative of the progress of the case and the outcome of the case handling, and provide explanations regarding the relevant circumstances.

Article 14 After determining the trial date for a criminal case of sexual assault against a minor, the people's court shall notify the minor victim and their legal representative of the trial time and place.

Article 15 When a people's court holds a trial for a criminal case of sexual assault against a minor, the minor victim or witness shall generally not be required to testify in court. Where it is truly necessary to testify in court, protective measures such as not revealing their appearance or real voice shall be adopted based on the circumstances of the case, or video recordings of the interview with the minor shall be played using video or other means, and technical measures shall also be applied to the video playback for protection.

Where the manner or content of questions raised in court by the defendant or their defense counsel is inappropriate and may cause physical or mental harm to the minor victim or witness, the presiding judge shall promptly stop them. Where the minor victim or witness exhibits panic, nervousness, agitation, resistance, or other circumstances that affect the normal conduct of the trial, the presiding judge shall declare a recess and take appropriate measures for emotional comfort and guidance, assessing the necessity for the minor victim or witness to continue testifying in court.

Article 16 When handling criminal cases of sexual assault against minors, personnel involved in the trial, prosecution, investigation, lawyers, and other relevant persons participating in the litigation or with knowledge of the case shall keep confidential the identity information of the minor and any materials from which identity information may be inferred, as well as details of the sexual assault.

Litigation documents made public shall not disclose the identity information of the minor or other materials from which identity information may be inferred, and the facts of the sexual assault must be narrated in an appropriate manner.

When case-handling personnel go to the schools, workplaces, or residences of the minor or their relatives to investigate and collect evidence, they shall avoid driving police vehicles, wearing uniforms, or adopting other methods that may reveal the identity of the minor or affect the minor's reputation or privacy.

Article 17 Where a person knows or should know that the other party is a female child under the age of 14 and commits sexual assault such as rape, it shall be determined that the person "knew" the other party to be a female child.

Where a person commits sexual assault such as rape against a victim under the age of 12, it shall be determined that the person "knew" the other party to be a female child.

Where the victim is between 12 and 14 years of age, and based on observations of physical development, speech and behavior, clothing characteristics, daily routine, etc., the victim may be a female child, and the person commits sexual assault such as rape, it shall be determined that the person "knew" the other party to be a female child.

Article 18 Where a crime of rape or indecency against a minor is committed in public places such as schools, swimming pools, children's playgrounds, or student dormitories, as long as there are multiple other persons present, regardless of whether the persons present actually saw the act, it may be determined as rape or indecency "in public" in accordance with the provisions of Article 236, paragraph 3, and Article 237 of the Criminal Law.

Article 19 Where a foreigner commits crimes such as rape or indecency against a minor within the territory of the People's Republic of China, when imposing punishment according to law, deportation may be imposed as a supplementary penalty. For acts that do not constitute a crime but constitute a violation of public security administration, or where the foreigner has a criminal record of sexual assault against a minor and is unsuitable to continue staying or residing in the country, the public security organ may apply a time limit for departure or deportation according to law.

Article 20 For adult criminals who commit sexual assault against minors, the conditions for applying commutation of sentence, parole, or temporary service of sentence outside prison shall be strictly controlled. Those placed under community correction shall be strictly supervised and controlled.

III. Evidence Collection and Examination

Article 21 When handling criminal cases of sexual assault against minors, public security organs shall, in accordance with legal procedures, promptly and comprehensively collect and fix evidence. They shall promptly conduct inspections and examinations of the places, objects, and persons related to the crime, and extract traces, physical evidence, and biological samples related to the case; promptly obtain documentary evidence such as accommodation, travel, and bank transaction records related to the case, audio-visual materials such as on-site surveillance video, and electronic data such as mobile phone text messages, instant communication records, social software records, mobile payment records, audio and video files, and cloud storage data. Where audio-visual materials or electronic data are lost due to improper custody, the original data storage unit shall be requested again, or submitted to a professional institution for technical recovery or restoration.

Article 22 Where the statement of a minor victim or the testimony of a minor witness mentions other criminal leads within the jurisdiction of the public security organ, the public security organ shall promptly investigate and verify; where such leads fall under the jurisdiction of other authorities, they shall be transferred to the authority with jurisdiction.

Where a person with convenient conditions for close contact with minors is suspected of committing a crime of sexual assault against minors, the public security organ shall take care to investigate other minors that the suspect may have had contact with, in order to fully ascertain the facts of the crime.

For sexual assault cases occurring near the suspect's residence or in the same or similar locations with similar modus operandi, where conditions for joinder are met, they shall be promptly joined for investigation to prevent omission of criminal facts.

Article 23 Interviews with minor victims shall be conducted in a "one-stop" evidence collection venue, the minor's residence, or other places that make the minor feel psychologically safe, and the legal representative shall be notified to be present. Where the legal representative cannot be present or is not suitable to be present, another suitable adult shall be notified to be present, and the relevant circumstances shall be recorded in the case file.

Interviews with minor victims shall be conducted in a gentle manner, using language that the minor can understand and accept. The principle of a single interview shall be adhered to, and repeated interviews shall be avoided as much as possible to prevent secondary harm. Where a re-interview is truly necessary, it shall be limited to verifying specific doubts.

Interviews with female minor victims shall be conducted by female staff.

Article 24 Interviews with minor victims shall be simultaneously audio- and video-recorded. The recording shall be continuous throughout the entire process, without selective recording, editing, or deletion. The audio and video shall be clear and stable, the interviewee's face shall be clearly discernible, and the recording shall truthfully reflect the state of the minor victim's responses during the interview. The recording shall be transferred along with the case file.

Article 25 Interviews with minor victims shall ascertain the facts and circumstances related to the sexual assault crime, including the victim's age and other identity information, the nature of the relationship with the criminal suspect or defendant, the method, time, location, frequency, and consequences of the assault.

During the interview, the victim shall be allowed to give a free narrative as much as possible, without leading questions, and the questions and the minor victim's answers shall be clearly recorded. The record shall preserve the linguistic characteristics of the minor and shall not be arbitrarily edited or summarized.

Article 26 Where the statements of minor victims and the confessions of criminal suspects or defendants contain details that are specific and could only be known by someone who experienced the event, including physical characteristics, behavioral characteristics, and environmental features, the case-handling authorities shall promptly fix the evidence through methods such as physical examination and on-site inspection.

Article 27 Evidence capable of proving the acquaintance and interaction between the minor victim and the criminal suspect or defendant, disputes, abnormal behavior, or special preferences, which is helpful for perfecting the chain of evidence and fully ascertaining all case circumstances, shall be comprehensively collected.

Article 28 Evidence capable of proving the psychological condition or behavioral manifestations of the minor victim after being sexually assaulted shall be comprehensively collected. Where the minor victim suffers psychological trauma, mental depression, or harmful consequences such as suicide or self-harm, prompt examination and appraisal shall be conducted.

Article 29 In determining a crime of sexual assault against a minor, the standard of proof of clear facts, reliable and sufficient evidence, and elimination of reasonable doubt shall be adhered to. The determination of case facts shall be based on evidence, combined with common sense and experience, taking into account the special nature of sexual assault cases and the physical and mental characteristics of minors, and the standard of proof shall be accurately understood and applied.

Article 30 When examining the statement of a minor victim, emphasis shall be placed on examining the time and background when the statement was made, the victim's age, cognitive, memory, and expressive abilities, whether physical and mental states affect the voluntariness and completeness of the statement, and whether the statement is consistent with other evidence without contradiction.

Where the statements of a young minor regarding the details of the assault are inconsistent, due consideration shall be given to their physical and mental characteristics, and a comprehensive assessment shall be made as to whether the main facts stated are objective and true.

Where a minor victim states details related to the criminal suspect, defendant, or the facts of the assault that could only be known by someone who experienced the event, and it can be ruled out that the statement was the result of being pointed at, induced, framed, or wrongly accused, the statement shall generally be admitted.

Where the content recorded in the interview record of a minor victim is inconsistent with the content recorded in the simultaneous audio-video recording of the interview, the determination shall be made accurately and objectively based on the simultaneous audio-video recording.

The examination of the testimony of minor witnesses shall be conducted in accordance with the preceding four paragraphs of this Article.

Article 31 In determining the true will of a minor victim aged 14 or above, the explicit expression of opposition or consent shall not be the sole evidence; a comprehensive determination shall be made in light of the minor victim's age, physical condition, behavioral manifestations before and after the assault, the relationship between the parties, the environment in which the case occurred, and the process of the incident.

IV. Protection and Assistance for Minor Victims

Article 32 When handling criminal cases of sexual assault against minors, people's courts, people's procuratorates, and public security organs shall, based on the actual needs of the minor victim and local conditions, coordinate with relevant departments to provide the minor victim with protective measures such as psychological counseling, temporary care, medical treatment, school transfer and placement, and economic assistance.

Article 33 After a criminal suspect arrives at the case, the case-handling personnel shall promptly ascertain whether the suspect has AIDS. Where the suspect is found to have AIDS, upon obtaining the consent of the guardian of the minor victim, they shall promptly cooperate or, together with the relevant departments, take protective measures such as blocking treatment for the minor victim.

Article 34 Where, in handling criminal cases of sexual assault against minors, people's courts, people's procuratorates, or public security organs discover that the parents or other guardians of a minor fail to perform their guardianship duties according to law or infringe upon the legitimate rights and interests of the minor, they shall issue a reprimand and urge in writing the parents to perform their guardianship duties according to law. Where necessary, the parents or other guardians of the minor may be ordered to receive family education guidance.

Article 35 Where a minor is sexually assaulted by their guardian, and other persons with guardianship qualifications, civil affairs departments, or other relevant units or organizations file an application with the people's court to revoke the guardianship qualifications and appoint a new guardian, the people's court shall support the application according to law.

Where the relevant individuals or organizations fail to file a timely application with the people's court to revoke the guardianship qualifications, the people's procuratorate may urge or support them to initiate litigation according to law.

Article 36 Where a minor suffers personal injury due to sexual assault and cannot obtain effective compensation in a timely manner, resulting in financial difficulties, the people's court, people's procuratorate, or public security organ may, together with relevant departments, prioritize consideration of relief.

V. Miscellaneous

Article 37 People's courts, people's procuratorates, public security organs, and judicial administrative organs shall actively promote the implementation of the mandatory reporting system for cases of harm to minors. Where failure to fulfill the reporting duty causes serious consequences, liability shall be pursued in accordance with the Law of the People's Republic of China on the Protection of Minors and other laws and regulations.

Article 38 People's courts, people's procuratorates, public security organs, and judicial administrative organs shall promote the establishment and improvement, according to law, of an entry inquiry system for information on sexual assault and other illegal acts in industries with close contact with minors, establish an information database on persons who have committed sexual assault and other illegal acts, and assist units with close contact with minors in conducting information inquiries.

Article 39 Case-handling authorities shall establish and improve a "one-stop" mechanism for handling cases and providing assistance for cases of sexual assault against minors. By setting up specialized venues, configuring dedicated equipment, improving work procedures, and introducing professional social forces, they shall, where possible, complete evidence collection work such as interviews, physical examinations, biological sample collection, and investigative identification in a single session, while simultaneously carrying out assistance and protection work.

VI. Supplementary Provisions

Article 40 These Opinions shall take effect on June 1, 2023. Upon the implementation of these Opinions, the "Opinions of the Supreme People's Court, Supreme People's Procuratorate, Ministry of Public Security, and Ministry of Justice on Severely Punishing Crimes of Sexual Assault against Minors According to Law" (Fa Fa [2013] No. 12) shall be simultaneously abolished.
